text:
sarah: FYI opened an RFC + PR for standardized GPU telemetry JSON + sampling rules to cut telemetry costs and make alerts/slo dashboards consistent. https://go/redwood/gpu-telemetry-rfc

ben: nice. main goals? reduce volume, make alerts reliable, and avoid shipping PII, right?

sarah: exactly. TL;DR: 1) canonical JSON schema for node/gpu events 2) field whitelist + deterministic hashing for identifiers 3) sampling rules per event type (prefix/cache/health) 4) migration plan + canary rollout to prod fleet

maria: can you paste an example event? want to see required vs optional fields

sarah: sure, short example:
```json
{
  "ts": "2026-11-03T15:12:01Z",
  "component": "gpu-agent",
  "node_id": "HASH(node-123)",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "instance_type": "p4d.24xlarge",
  "gpu_index": 0,
  "gpu_model": "A100-80GB",
  "metrics": {"gpu_util": 87, "mem_used_mb": 23856, "temp_c": 72},
  "event_type": "periodic_telemetry.v1",
  "sampled": "0.1"
}
```

ben: looks sane. for node_id we should use HMAC with per-customer salt so same node across infra still cannot be reversed. add note in RFC

sarah: yes, RFC recommends HMAC-SHA256 with KMS-managed salt; we already have k8s sidecars that can do it at emit time

tom: for alerts/dashboards we need region, availability_zone, and fleet_pool tag. also include model_variant for running jobs so we can correlate perf regressions

sarah: agreed, adding fleet_pool and job_model as optional fields. want to avoid per-request payloads though (keep telemetry coarse)

jess: sampling rules: can we stratify by job priority? low-priority jobs get higher sampling. also keep all anomaly events (oom, hw-failure) unsampled

sarah: yep. proposal: periodic telemetry sampled (0.1 default), prefix/cache events sampled higher (0.5), alerts and failures unsampled. and a burst window: if anomaly rate > threshold, temporarily raise sampling to 1.0 for affected nodes

ben: what about logs that might contain command line args or user-provided app labels? need a redact list and field-level allowlist
maria: +1. suggest we add a lint step in the pipeline that rejects events with disallowed keys like "cmdline", "user_email", "api_key"

sarah: RFC includes a JSON schema and a validator in the agent. pipeline will run a schema-lint + PII-redact hook. we'll also ship a migration-mode where invalid fields are dropped and flagged rather than rejected for 2 weeks before enforcement

ops-bot: alert: gpu-memory-usage (p95) > 90% on pool-gpu-west-3 for 3m (node gpu-node-112).

jess: ack, I'll take a look, but that alert should be tuned to avoid noise during rollout; maybe bump to 95% for initial weeks

sarah: good catch. plan is to: 1) create new telemetry schema metrics-based alerts in a separate alertgroup 2) mirror old alerts to avoid gaps 3) run a 4-week canary in us-west-2 with relaxed thresholds 4) iterate thresholds based on false-positive rate

tom: add runbook links in alert annotations pointing to the new telemetry runbook + rollback steps
sarah: will add. owners: jess + ben for alert tuning, tom for dashboard changes, maria for pipeline/PII, and me for schema/agent work

deploy-bot: rfc PR merged to canary branch, created canary rollout job: rollout/gpu-telemetry-canary (50 nodes in us-west-2).

ben: timeline? when does canary start?
sarah: starting next Tue 09:00 UTC, canary window 72h, then progressive rollout if error/fp rates < 5%. will post a brief schedule in #eng-runtime before deploy

maria: anything needed from infra? need k8s-sidecar image update and KMS permission for HMAC keys
sarah: infra: need sidecar image promotion and KMS policy update. infra-owners, is that doable in the window?

ben: infra ok on KMS change, will coordinate with security for key rotation notes. sidecar image build queued

jess: I'll prepare dashboard copy + a comparison panel (old vs new telemetry) so we can eyeball differences during canary

tom: also add cost estimate in RFC: expected 30-40% telemetry egress reduction for telemetry store and ~15% less Prometheus remote write after metric rollups

sarah: added cost numbers to RFC, plus expected SLO impact (none). will update RFC w/ tom's dashboard plan and the exact alert thresholds after canary

ben: sounds good. quick nits in PR: rename field "sampled" -> "sampling_rate" and make numeric. also prefer snake_case for keys to match our other logs

sarah: will update PR. thanks everyone :rocket:

jess: ack. I'll post an ETA for dashboard work by EOD

ops-bot: NOTE: scheduled maintenance for logging-ingest in us-west-2 at 2026-11-10T02:00:00Z may affect sample rates briefly.

sarah: noted — will avoid starting canary during that window.

ben: cool. queueing follow-ups: 1) schema update PR, 2) sidecar image, 3) canary job, 4) dashboard diffs, 5) runbook + alert annotation. will track in the RFC issue

sarah: thanks all. ping here if you see any blocker before next Tue
